title: Solving sin^2(theta) = 3/4 on [0, 2*pi]
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Solve the trigonometric equation \sin^2\theta = 3/4 for the angle \theta in the interval 0 \le \theta \le 2\pi.

steps.title: Take Square Roots of Both Sides
steps.explanation: Extract both positive and negative square roots to obtain two elementary trigonometric equations: sin theta = sqrt(3)/2 and sin theta = -sqrt(3)/2.
steps.why: An equation u^2 = c (with c > 0) has two real solutions u = +sqrt(c) and u = -sqrt(c).

steps.title: Find Solutions to sin(theta) = +sqrt(3)/2 in [0, 2*pi]
steps.explanation: With reference angle pi/3, sine is positive in Quadrants I and II, yielding theta = pi/3 and theta = pi - pi/3 = 2*pi/3.

steps.title: Find Solutions to sin(theta) = -sqrt(3)/2 in [0, 2*pi]
steps.explanation: Sine is negative in Quadrants III and IV with reference angle pi/3, yielding theta = pi + pi/3 = 4*pi/3 and theta = 2*pi - pi/3 = 5*pi/3.
steps.why: All four angles in [0, 2*pi] with reference angle pi/3 satisfy |sin theta| = sqrt(3)/2.
